primitives.name: Cheap Agent Execution Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Operating rule: cheap agents execute, the expensive one only steers Every research and authoring task in this plan runs on Sonnet-class subagents with a written brief and a fixed output path.
primitives.assumptions: Agent execution is deterministic within defined brief scope; orchestrator steering is non-computational.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when agent output deviates from fixed path without conflict resolution.

layer2.mapping: Orchestrator's steering function maps to agent execution space via prompt structure; both operate under same semantic constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Agent output validation against fixed path specification.

primitives.name: Design System Synchronization
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Phase 0: the design system Claude Design builds with (built, upload pending) `/design-sync` converts the real `apps/web` components into the Claude Design format so every screen the design agent produces is made of shipping parts.
primitives.assumptions: Component fidelity preserved during format conversion; sync process is lossless.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Upload fails if component set is incomplete or unverified.

layer2.mapping: Sync pipeline generates semantic kernel of UI components; kernel enables cross-platform rendering consistency.
layer2.telemetry: Component count and render check status from batch validation.

primitives.name: Steering Function Validation
primitives.verbatim_quote: The orchestrating session (Fable) only writes briefs, reads results, resolves conflicts and validates names against the build.
primitives.assumptions: Orchestrator operates exclusively on metadata and result validation; no direct computation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Conflict resolution fails if briefs lack clarity or results exceed scope.

layer2.mapping: Orchestrator's validation logic mirrors build structure; both validate naming consistency.
layer2.telemetry: Conflict resolution log and name validation metrics.

reasoning_traces.think:
The delegation hierarchy enforces a strict separation of labor where low-cost agents execute tasks based on fixed prompts while the orchestrator steers by writing briefs and validating outputs. This creates a dual-layered system: one of execution governed by deterministic prompts and another of control through validation and conflict resolution. The design system synchronization phase ensures that all components used in the design process are directly traceable to production code, maintaining fidelity and enabling seamless integration. The orchestrator's role is limited to high-level coordination, avoiding micro-management of implementation details such as string manipulation or contrast ratio calculations. This architecture supports scalability and reduces error propagation by isolating complex operations within specialized agents.
